meaning:
μισέω, -ῶ
[in LXX chiefly for שָׂנֵא ;]
to hate: with accusative of person(s) Mat.5:43 24:10, Luk.1:71 6:22, 27 19:14, Jhn.7:7 15:18-19, 23-26 17:14, Tit.3:3, 1Jn.2:9 Jn 2:11 Jn 3:13 Jn 3:15 Jn 4:20 Rev.17:16; pass., Mat.10:22 24:9, Mrk.13:13, Luk.21:17; with accusative of thing(s), Jhn.3:20, Rom.7:15, Eph.5:29, Heb.1:9, Ju 23, Rev.2:6; pass., Rev.18:2. As the Heb. שָׂנֵא is sometimes found with the modified sense of indifference to or relative disregard for one thing in comparison with another (cf. Gen.29:30-31, Deu.21:15-16, Mal.1:3) so prob. μ. in the foll.: Mat.6:24, Luk.14:26 16:13, Jhn.12:25, Rom.9:13" (LXX) .†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: “You have heard that it was said, ‘You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’
You will be hated by all men for my name’s sake, but he who endures to the end will be saved.
salvation from our enemies and from the hand of all who hate us;
For everyone who does evil hates the light, and doesn’t come to the light, lest his works would be exposed.
For I don’t know what I am doing. For I don’t practice what I desire to do; but what I hate, that I do.
For no man ever hated his own flesh; but nourishes and cherishes it, even as the Lord also does the assembly;
For we were also once foolish, disobedient, deceived, serving various lusts and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another.
You have loved righteousness and hated iniquity; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your fellows.”
